def t02_totais(self) -> Resultado:
    sc = self.sc.copy()
    sc["k"] = sc["cargo"].map(VAGAS_POR_CARGO).fillna(1).astype(int)
    sc["esperado"] = sc["k"] * sc["comp"]
    sc["delta"] = sc["total"] - sc["esperado"]
    d = sc[(sc["delta"] != 0) & sc["comp"].notna()]
    tab = montar_sinais(d, "T02", "anomalia", "soma_votos", d["total"].values, d["esperado"].values,
                        detalhe=("Δ=" + d["delta"].astype(str) + "; k=" + d["k"].astype(str)).values)
    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
        razao = (sc["total"] / sc["comp"]).round(3)
    modal = (sc.assign(r=razao).groupby("cargo")["r"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0] if len(s.mode()) else np.nan))
    contagem = sc.groupby("cargo").size()
    self.meta["k_validacao"] = [{"cargo": int(k), "boletins": int(contagem[k]), "razao_modal": float(modal[k]),
                                 "k": VAGAS_POR_CARGO.get(int(k), 1)} for k in modal.index]
    return Resultado("T02", unidades=len(sc), sinalizados=len(tab), tabela=tab)

**Test 15 — Election Fingerprint (Klimek)**

**Method.** For each section: turnout t = turnout / eligible voters; vote share s = candidate votes / valid votes. Two-dimensional histograms (election fingerprints; Klimek et al., 2012) are produced per candidate, in aggregate and by state, and the following are computed: Pearson correlation between t and s weighted by eligible voters; number of sections in the upper-right corner (t ≥ 90% and s ≥ 90%) and the ratio between the observed number and the number expected under independence between turnout and vote share within each reference group (stratified expectation, which neutralizes the pooling of regions with different profiles). q: Nature of the document and caveats

**Section 1 — Nature of the document and caveats**

States that it is an exploratory statistical analysis, not an official document, and that it attributes no conduct to anyone.

**Section 2 — Authorship and technical responsibility**

Identifies the author, specialty, place of execution and Instagram.

**Section 3 — Executive summary**

Overall numbers, file integrity, flagged sections and the table with the 15 tests. It also explains how to check your machine.

**Section 4 — Scope, data sources and coverage**

TSE sources used and the coverage table by state (file, records and sections).

q: Data integrity and digital chain of custody
a:

SHA-512 of each input file, check against the TSE official hash and the manifest hash.

**Section 6 — Computing environment and timeline**

Processing start, end and duration, system, Python, libraries, cores and memory.

**Section 7 — Pre-processing and quality control**

How the CSVs are read, how TSE sentinel values are handled, the section key and the validation of k (votes per voter).

Unit of analysis, reference groups, beta-binomial model, multiple-comparison adjustment, deterministic tests and parameter table.

**Section 9 — Results by test**

One subsection per test (9.1 to 9.15): objective, method, criterion, limitations, result and the full list of machines.

Sections flagged by two or more distinct test families: higher verification priority.

Sections, flagged sections and percentage in each state.

What the analysis does not examine and why a flag does not indicate the cause.

Determinism check, execution command and SHA-512 of each output file.

Cited papers and standards: Benjamini–Hochberg, Mebane, Beber–Scacco, Klimek, Skellam, Ridout and others.

q: what does ballot box report mean
what does boletim de urna mean
a: **BU** — Document the voting machine prints and publishes at the end of voting, with eligible voters, turnout, abstentions and the votes for each candidate, blank and null in the section.
**section** — Group of voters who vote on the same machine. It is the smallest unit of the result.
**zone** — Administrative division of the Electoral Justice within a state. The section is numbered within the zone.
**UF** — State or Federal District. At the TSE, ZZ is the code for Abroad.
**eligible voters** — Voters entitled to vote in that section.
**turnout** — Voters who voted in the section.
**abstention** — Eligible voters who did not vote. Eligible = turnout + abstentions.
**valid votes** — Candidate and party-list votes. Blank and null votes are excluded.
**blank vote** — Vote cast with the BLANK key. In the BU it is option 95. It is not valid.
**null vote** — Vote for a non-existent number. In the BU it is option 96. It is not valid.
**annulled vote** — Vote annulled and tallied separately (option 97). It counts in the total but not among valid votes.
**party-list vote** — Vote only for the party number, in proportional offices (Deputy).
**vote option** — Each option that receives votes in the BU: candidate, party, blank (95), null (96) or annulled (97).
**aggregated section** — Section that voted together with another (the main one). Its votes appear under the main section's number.
**polling place** — Building (usually a school) that houses several sections. Test 8 compares sections at the same place.
**contingency machine** — Spare machine that replaces a faulty one. It is a planned procedure; test 12 checks that it is on the official list with the right load.
**load code** — Identifier of each machine's preparation (software load). It lets one check that the machine used is the planned one.
**CESP** — TSE files stating which machine was expected in each section and which ones are contingency machines. Used in test 12.
**counting board** — When voting is on paper ballots or data is recovered, counting is done by the board. Test 12 records this as informational.
**biometrics** — Fingerprint identification. The BU reports how many voters with biometrics were cleared without a fingerprint reading (test 10).
**hash** — Code computed from a file's content. If a single byte changes, the hash changes. It proves the file was not altered.
**SHA-512** — Hash algorithm (FIPS 180-4) used by the TSE in .sha512 files and by the engine to check the files.
**SHA-256** — Hash algorithm used on the analytical core for the determinism check.
**manifest** — SHA-512 of the sorted list 'name;size;sha512' of the input files. It identifies the analyzed data set.
**analytical core** — File dados/nucleo_analitico.json with the results of the 15 analyses, without date, time or duration. Its SHA-256 proves that the same input gives the same result.
**determinism** — On the first run the engine records the core's SHA-256 (baseline). Every new run with the same files is compared to it; if it differs, the report shows an alert.
**p-value** — Probability of seeing a result this extreme if the reference model is right. The smaller, the rarer.
**q-value** — p-value adjusted by Benjamini–Hochberg for the thousands of comparisons. The engine flags when q < 0.01.

q: what does false discovery rate mean
a: **FDR** — With hundreds of thousands of sections, some look rare just by chance. The Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment limits the expected share of false alarms to 1% (0.01).
**beta-binomial** — Model for counts (a candidate's votes out of n) that allows sections to vary more than a simple draw. Mean and spread are estimated in the reference group.
**overdispersion** — Real variation larger than the binomial model predicts, due to differences between electorates. The beta-binomial model and the φ factor correct for it.
**intraclass correlation** — The beta-binomial parameter ρ that measures how much sections in a group differ. Bounded between 0.000001 and 0.5.
**reference group** — Set of comparable sections: zone within municipality (≥ 20 sections); otherwise municipality, zone, state and round.
**leave-one-out** — The tested section is removed from its group's calculation, so it does not mask itself.
**robust z** — Distance of a value from the group median, measured in median absolute deviations (MAD). Resistant to extreme values.

**Benford** — Frequency pattern of digits in many number sets. The engine does not use the 1st digit (unsuitable for per-section votes) and, for the 2nd digit, uses a simulated reference; the Benford mean (4.187) is shown only for comparison.
**Monte Carlo** — Generating many random results with a model to obtain the expected distribution. In tests 13 and 14 there are 50 replicas with fixed seed 20261004.
**chi-square** — Statistic measuring the distance between the observed and expected distributions (9 degrees of freedom in the digit tests).
**election fingerprint** — 2D plot of turnout × vote share per section (Klimek et al., 2012). A pile-up in the upper-right corner deserves inspection.
**anomaly** — An arithmetically impossible (tests 1 and 2) or statistically improbable result for its context. It indicates priority for document verification.
**informational event** — Occurrence recorded for transparency that did not meet the anomaly criterion (e.g. official contingency machine, delayed opening).
**raw occurrences** — How many times the event happened before the statistical criterion (e.g. all sections with 100% for one candidate).
**convergent** — Section flagged by two or more distinct test families. Coupled tests count once: 1 and 2 (arithmetic); 3, 6 and 8 (concentration).

q: what does digital vote record mean
a: **RDV** — Machine file with every recorded vote, shuffled and without identifying the voter. This audit does not examine it.
**logjez** — Signed digital files of the machine (.logjez = event log; .imgbu = BU image; .bu = report). Recommended for checking flagged sections; not part of this analysis.
**e-Título** — Voter document (physical or app) showing the zone and section.
**DuckDB** — Columnar analytical database the engine uses to read the full CSVs, without sampling, using all cores.
**Abroad** — Sections of Brazilians abroad (code ZZ). They vote in local time and are excluded from the national aggregate of test 15.
**time zone** — Opening and closing times in the BU are in local time. That is why an Acre machine opens at 6 a.m. local (8 a.m. Brasília). The engine infers each municipality's time zone.
**machine type** — Machine status in the BU: tallied, not tallied, annulled, annulled and tallied separately or not installed. Types other than 'tallied' are anomalies in test 12.
**in-transit voter** — Voter who voted outside their section, entitled to vote for President only. It explains presidential turnout higher than state-level turnout.
**Mebane** — Second-digit test (2BL), proposed by Walter Mebane (2006, 2008). It is test 13.
**Beber-Scacco** — Last-digit test (Beber and Scacco, 2012): numbers made up by people repeat certain endings. It is test 14.
